questions: Is the main reason for your visit related to a problem with your legs?
Is the problem affecting only one leg?
Have you noticed any swelling in the affected leg?
Is there any redness or warmth over the area?
Do you have any open wounds or ulcers on your legs?
Have you had a fever in the past few days?
Have you recently been confined to bed or had reduced mobility?
Have you had recent surgery in the past month?
Do you have a history of cancer?
Do you have a history of blood clots?
Do you have a history of varicose veins or leg swelling?
Do you have pain in the leg when walking that improves with rest?
Do you have numbness or tingling in your feet?
Have you noticed any skin discoloration (brownish or darkening) on your ankles?
Are you currently taking any blood-thinning medication?
orders: Bedside examination of the skin lesions to assess distribution, palpability (palpable vs non-palpable purpura), and blanching on diascopy
Complete blood count with differential and platelet count
Prothrombin time and international normalized ratio
